# `silk/toml_output`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

TOML document and value output through the ambient Writer.

## When to use
Use [`TomlOutput.write`](#TomlOutput.impl.write) for an owned TOML document. Unsupported scalar spellings and
container shapes fail before the first write. Writer failures may leave an accepted prefix.

## Examples
### Write a parsed document
```silk
import silk.allocator as Allocators {Allocator, OutOfMemoryError}
import silk.effect as Effects {Effect}
import silk.toml_output as Outputs {TomlOutput}
import silk.toml_scanner as Scanners {TomlError}
import silk.toml_value as Values {Toml}
import silk.usize as Sizes
import silk.writer as Writers {Writer, WriterError}

struct Count {
  bytes: usize
}

effect fn writeAll(self: &mut Count, data: &[u8]) -> () ! WriterError {
  self.bytes = self.bytes + data.length
}

effect fn flush(self: &mut Count) -> () ! WriterError {
  return ()
}

impl Writer for Count {
  writeAll: Count.writeAll
  flush: Count.flush
}

effect fn write() -> i32 ! TomlError | OutOfMemoryError | WriterError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let document = run Toml.parse(b"name = \"Ada\"\n")
    |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  let mut output = Count {bytes: Sizes.ZERO}
  run TomlOutput.write(&document)
    |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
    |> Effect.provideMut<Writer>(&mut output)
  if output.bytes > Sizes.ZERO {
    return 0
  }
  return 1
}

effect fn recover(error: TomlError | OutOfMemoryError | WriterError) -> i32 {
  return 2
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  return run Effect.catchAll(write(), recover)
}
```

Import as `TomlOutput` with `import silk.toml_output { TomlOutput }`.

### Associated function `write`

```silk
pub effect fn write(document: &Value)
    -> () ! TomlError | OutOfMemoryError | WriterError ? &mut Allocator | &mut Writer
```

Writes a complete document, preserving table and array-of-tables structure.

#### Details
Invalid scalar text or container structure fails before the first write.
Writer failure can leave an accepted prefix. This operation does not flush the Writer.
